name: Argha Dey IoT Firmware Analysis Methodology
description: 4-stage IoT methodology: Recon/Enumeration → Firmware Acquisition → Firmware Static Analysis → Binary/Runtime Exploitation. Includes exam-day tips, firmware header cheat-sheet, question-pattern mapping, and full tool reference.
examHabits: Always run binwalk before anything else on any .bin file - it answers 60-70% of firmware questions in one shot
Check target locale/date format (date command) before answering date-formatted questions - labs use YYYY-DD-MM traps
If binwalk shows nothing → suspect encryption; confirm with -E (entropy) flag - high flat entropy + no signatures = encrypted
Don't install tools on the target box - pivot file via Python HTTP server + wget (faster, no root/apt needed)
Recursive/forced extraction (eM --dd='.*') is fallback when default binwalk doesn't reveal FS name - walk nested folders manually
Distinguish standard vs custom directories - questions want non-standard folders (pwnable dir), not /etc, /bin, /usr
For device-identification questions: browser page title + quick Google search is fastest (e.g. 'dsp-w215' → HNAP → SOAP family)
Always start binary exploitation with file (arch + stripped) → readelf -h/-l → gdb-peda → qemu-<arch>-static if non-native
quickRef: binwalk FileOne.bin; binwalk -eM --dd='.*' FileOne.bin; file <extracted>; strings | grep -i busybox|gcc|linux version; sqlite3 config.sqlite .dump | grep -i <device>

decisionPoints.action: nmap -sCV -p- <ip> — note SSH banner (OpenSSH tells base OS/Linux kernel), http admin panels, /cgi-bin/
decisionPoints.fallback: ssh <user>@<target-ip> with supplied creds or hydra brute force

decisionPoints.action: Method A: python3 -m http.server 8080 (on target); wget http://<target-ip>:8080/<file>.bin (on attacker). Method B: scp user@<target>:/path/to/file.bin . (Method C: cat/base64 exfil over HTTP if shell only)
decisionPoints.fallback: If binwalk not on target: pivot the file rather than installing tools on target

decisionPoints.action: file FileOne.bin — if 'data', it's a generic firmware blob, not recognizable filetype
decisionPoints.fallback: binwalk FileOne.bin — scan for embedded signatures

decisionPoints.action: binwalk -eM FileOne.bin (recursive extraction + Matryoshka); if no signatures, try binwalk -eM --dd='.*' FileOne.bin
decisionPoints.fallback: binwalk -E FileOne.bin for entropy analysis (detect encryption)

decisionPoints.action: Treat as encrypted — no further unpacking possible
decisionPoints.fallback: If entropy high but gzip/LZMA signatures present: it's compressed, not encrypted

decisionPoints.action: cd squashfs-root; ls; look for non-standard dirs (pwnable/, custom services); grep -Rin 'passwd=' .; grep -Rin 'root:' . | grep -v Binary; cat etc/passwd; cat etc/shadow
strings <binary> | grep -i 'busybox|gcc|linux version' for BusyBox/GCC/kernel version banners; find . -type f -regextype posix-extended -regex '.*/[a-z]{5}_[a-z]{6}' for flag-named files
decisionPoints.fallback: file <extracted_file> (hex filename = offset; cross-ref binwalk decimal/hex columns)

decisionPoints.condition: Web admin panel identified via page title
decisionPoints.action: Open Login.html in browser, note title (e.g. DSP-W215 → Google → HNAP/SOAP family protocol)

decisionPoints.condition: ARM/MIPS/Blackfin binary found in pwnable dir
decisionPoints.action: file <binary> (arch + stripped state); readelf -h (entry point, machine); readelf -l (segments, GNU_STACK for NX, GNU_RELRO); checksec --file=<binary>
decisionPoints.fallback: qemu-arm-static -g 1234 ./binary &; gdb-multiarch; set architecture arm; target remote localhost:1234

decisionPoints.action: gdb: break main; run; p system; find /bin/sh; p/x <addr1> - <addr2> for ret2libc offset; check protections for exploit strategy
qemu-mips-static ./binary OR qemu-arm-static ./binary; qemu-arm -g 1234 ./binary & + gdb-multiarch for debugging
decisionPoints.fallback: patchelf to set local libc/interpreter matching remote target

decisionPoints.action: binwalk file.bin → 'blocksize: NNNNN bytes'
binwalk file.bin → 'CPU ARCH' in uImage header line OR file <extracted_binary>
strings <binary> | grep 'linux version'; binwalk → uImage 'Linux-XX.X.XX' string
decisionPoints.fallback: readelf -h for entry point + program headers

decisionPoints.action: binwalk description line: Squashfs / JFFS2 / CRAMFS
Cross-ref binwalk decimal/hex column, or the file's own numeric name (hex offset)
sqlite3 config.sqlite .dump | grep -i <devicename>
strings busybox | grep -i busybox; strings <binary> | grep -i gcc
find . -iname passwd; cat etc/passwd; cat etc/shadow; grep for root: inside extracted files
grep webroot for DeviceID:/title tags; or config DB dump; or browser page title + Google

cd usr/local (third-party services like samba); cd pwnable (custom exploit-dev challenge dirs = attack surface); cd www/www-ro (web front-end, check .cgi/.asp/.html); cd etc (passwd/shadow, network configs); cd mnt (config.sqlite, persistent storage)
